coredata.dc:title: Unveiling the cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on tricalcium silicate (C3S) during cement kiln co-processing hazardous wastes containing Cu
coredata.dc:creator: Da, Yongqi
He, Tingshu
Shi, Chen
coredata.dc:description: Fluorine (F) from fluorite mineralizer and copper (Cu) would be introduced together into raw meals during cement kiln co-processing hazardous wastes containing Cu, unfortunately the cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on the properties of cement clinker are still vague, it directly restricts the resource utilization of these wastes in the cement industry. Therefore, the cooperation effects of fluorine (CaF2) and copper (CuO) on the formation and properties of tricalcium silicate (C3S) were unveiled. The results indicated that a small cooperation addition of CuO could reduce distinctly f-CaO content of C3S doped with CaF2, and its burnability would be promoted notably, the immobilization of fluorine and copper in doped C3S also were promoted. Compared with C3S doped with CaF2, a cooperation addition of CuO and CaF2 further improved the formation of C3S grains and increased the structural symmetry of C3S crystal. The cooperation effects triggered the diffraction peaks for C3S polymorphisms to shift right, and induced the visible defects on the surface of C3S grains. In the current incorporation amounts of CaF2 and CuO into C3S, F- and Cu2+ would dissolve in its structure possibly by the replacement of O2– and Ca2+ respectively. CaF2 addition accelerated the initial hydration, but postponed the later hydration of C3S. The initial hydration was further accelerated by a cooperation addition of CuO, and its effects would be quite different if changing cooperation amounts of CaF2, accelerating or decelerating the hydration process of doped C3S relied on the cooperation amounts of CaF2 and CuO. The findings in this work would be expected to provide a promising solution to reduce the large energy consumption and CO2 emission in cement industry.

ce:abstract-sec.ce:simple-para: Fluorine (F) from fluorite mineralizer and copper (Cu) would be introduced together into raw meals during cement kiln co-processing hazardous wastes containing Cu, unfortunately the cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on the properties of cement clinker are still vague, it directly restricts the resource utilization of these wastes in the cement industry. Therefore, the cooperation effects of fluorine (CaF2) and copper (CuO) on the formation and properties of tricalcium silicate (C3S) were unveiled. The results indicated that a small cooperation addition of CuO could reduce distinctly f-CaO content of C3S doped with CaF2, and its burnability would be promoted notably, the immobilization of fluorine and copper in doped C3S also were promoted. Compared with C3S doped with CaF2, a cooperation addition of CuO and CaF2 further improved the formation of C3S grains and increased the structural symmetry of C3S crystal. The cooperation effects triggered the diffraction peaks for C3S polymorphisms to shift right, and induced the visible defects on the surface of C3S grains. In the current incorporation amounts of CaF2 and CuO into C3S, F- and Cu2+ would dissolve in its structure possibly by the replacement of O2– and Ca2+ respectively. CaF2 addition accelerated the initial hydration, but postponed the later hydration of C3S. The initial hydration was further accelerated by a cooperation addition of CuO, and its effects would be quite different if changing cooperation amounts of CaF2, accelerating or decelerating the hydration process of doped C3S relied on the cooperation amounts of CaF2 and CuO. The findings in this work would be expected to provide a promising solution to reduce the large energy consumption and CO2 emission in cement industry.

ce:section.ce:para: Nowadays, people constantly benefit from the visible convenience brought by the high-quality development of science and technology, concurrently they are also subject to the knotty burden of the enormous waste generation and the latent environmental contamination brought by the booming growth of the global population and the ever-intensifying industrialization. The World Bank data revealed that the global generation of wastes in 2016 was about 2.00 billion tons, it will probably crept up to 2.60 billion tons in 2030 and 3.40 billion tons in 2050 [1]. Take the example of China, the 3.28 billion tons of industrial solid waste, 173 million tons of municipal solid waste and 25 million tons of sludge were produced only in 2016 [2]. Roughly 77.00% of the solid wastes were presently still disposed in the open landfills or were transported to the waste burning facilities [3], in addition to the extensive occupation of valuable land resource, it would make a big threat to air, soil and water environment [4].

Cement has been recognized as the most widely applied artificial materials in the modern buildings, traffic infrastructures and marine constructions [5]. It is reported the cement production of China was 2.77 billion tons in 2018 with an increasing rate of 3.0% per year [6], and its production already surpassed more than half of the global cement production [7]. The tremendous demand of cement not only bring huge challenges, but also take good opportunities, the shortage of natural raw materials of cement production, the great energy consumption and the large CO2 emissions triggered a consideration of the utilization of solid waste as alternative raw materials in cement production [8]. The wastes from different industries containing calcium, silicon, aluminum and iron could be introduced as alternative raw materials into cement raw meals, till now cement kiln co-processing has been a very promising harmless treatment and resource reutilization for the industrial solid wastes [9], municipal solid waste [10], sludge [11], and even the hazardous wastes [12–15]. Nevertheless, some new problems gradually appeared during the co-processing process. Heavy metals and some impurity elements in these wastes might combine with cement clinker mineral phases during sintering at high temperature, theses impurities might alter the burnability, mineral compositions, and microstructure of produced clinker [16,17], then could affect the hydration characteristic and macro properties of produced cement [18,19], so the sufficient attention and discussion on the above problems is pivotal to implement waste utilization in cement kiln co-processing.

Copper (Cu) is a common hazardous element in the solid wastes, sludge and fossil fuels, e.g. copper slags [20], copper tailings [21], municipal solid waste [22], sewage sludge [23], and the polluted soil [24]. It has been realized that copper Cu would mainly be incorporated into the clinker minerals with cement kiln co-processing Cu-containing wastes, and it would influence on the hydration process and mechanical properties of the clinker [25]. Kakali et al. [26] revealed that CuO is beneficial to stimulate the combination of free CaO in the clinker at sintering temperature of 1000℃～1300℃, and reduced clinkering temperature by about 50℃. Ma et al. [13] reported that CuO increased the formation and growth of C3S, and R-type C3S would be transformed into M3 type. The addition of CuO more than 1.00% would prolong the induction period of hydration, accelerate the initial reaction rate and acceleration period. Some researchers discussed that the delayed effect of CuO on hydration process mainly due to formation of Cu(OH)2 [27] or Ca2(OH)4 ·4Cu(OH)2·2H2O [28], it might enter the covering layer of hydration products on the surface of clinker minerals and inhibit further hydration. Additionally, Shih et al. [29] and Chen et al. [30] pointed that Cu2+ in the wastes would be solidified in hydration products with trace amounts of leaching toxicity below the leaching limit when the CuO doped clinker hydrated.

Fluorine (F) is the widely applied mineralizer in cement kiln, and also is the major pollutants of the semiconductor-industry sludge [31], fluoride wastewater sludge [32], and the stainless-steel pickling sludge [33]. CaF2 could effectively reduce the clinkering temperature by 50℃～100℃, stimulate the formation of clinker minerals especially for alite, and lessen the large consumption of coal [34–35]. Yamashita et al. [36] discovered that the addition of CaF2 in clinker could decrease the viscosity and surface tension of the liquid melt state, the solid-state diffusion would be enhanced effectively. Tran et al. [37] and Boughanmi et al. [38] proposed that F- of CaF2 could be preferentially incorporated into C3S structure with the substitution of the O2− not linked to silicon, an excess of positive charge by F- substitute O2– would be compensated by the calcium vacancy, then it would change the hydration characteristic of the doped C3S by changing its polymorph symmetry and introducing the crystal defects [39]. Emanuelson et al. [40] and Moir et al. [41] realized that the doping amounts of F in clinker should be 0.25%～0.60% to obtain proper properties of clinker, once excessive fluoride was incorporated, the hydration process would be postponed and the properties would be weakened.

However, it is inevitable that fluorine from fluorite mineralizer and copper would be introduced into raw meals at the same time when the wastes containing copper were co-processed in current cement kiln. The introduced F and Cu will participate clinkering reactions in cement clinker preparation, however, it is still unknown that the effects of simultaneous existence of F and Cu on the formation and properties of cement clinker minerals, in addition, the related researches about the above concerns were rare so far. Tring to addressing and comprehending the collective influences of F and Cu on cement clinker is a key issue to promote the co-processing wastes containing copper in cement kiln.

Thereupon, a main mineral of Portland cement clinker of tricalcium silicate (C3S) was chose as the research object, CaF2 and CuO were used as the source of F and Cu to simulate the clinking process. The cooperation effects of F and Cu on the formation, C3S polymorphisms, microstructures, and hydration process of C3S would be explored by XRD, SEM-EDS, XPS and isothermal heat flow calorimetry. These findings in this work are expected to provide theoretical supports to the comprehensive utilization of hazardous Cu-containing wastes in cement kiln.

The doped and undoped C3S samples were synthesized using a conventional solid-state sintering method [42]. The starting materials used are all analytical grade chemical reagents SiO2, CaCO3, CaF2, and CuO, and the starting material compositions of doped C3S samples were presented in Table 1 . The analytical grade CaCO3 and SiO2 were the starting materials for undoped C3S, the analytical grade CaF2 and CuO were dopants to prepare doped C3S, in addition, the doping amounts of CaF2 in C3S were 1.00%, 1.50% and 2.00%, the cooperation doping amounts of CuO in C3S were 0.25%, 0.50% and 1.00%. The previous study [43] already noted that the introduction of CaF2 would bring a spare calcium atom into the structure of C3S, which would break the original chemical form of C3S, thus the actual addition of CaCO3 should subtract the equivalent CaCO3 caused by addition of CaF2.

Firstly, the analytical grade CaCO3 and SiO2 powders (the mole ratio CaO/SiO2 is 3:1) with/without CaF2 and CuO would be fully mixed with ethanol (solid liquid ratio is 1:10) in a magnetic stirrer for 24 h, and then the mixed paste was dried at 50℃ for 24 h. Secondly, these powders couple with 10.0% ethanol were pressed into cylindrical pellets (diameter is 50 mm and height is 20 mm) under 40.0 MPa. The prepared pellets with different compositions were calcined in tubular high temperature furnace XCSL-16–17 V at 1500℃, the calcination procedures were showed in Table 2
[43]. After every calcination cycle, free lime (f-CaO) contents of the calcined C3S samples were tested until it is less than 1.00%. If f-CaO content was beyond 1.00%, the air-quenched calcined samples would be reground to powders, pelletized and calcined again. The well-prepared calcined C3S samples would be selected to crack into small pieces for the measurements of SEM-EDS, and some other pieces would be ground into powders to pass through 75 μm sieve for the tests of burnability, immobilization ratios, XRD, XPS and heat flow.

The f-CaO content is a good indicator for the burnability of doped C3S samples, the less amounts would reveal good solid state reaction between C2S and CaO. The f-CaO content of C3S samples was measured by the ethanol-glycol method using F Ca-2008 free lime measuring instrument. The immobilization ratios of Cu and F element in the samples were measured according to the methods published by Yang et al. [44].

Mineral compositions of prepared C3S samples were tested by X-Ray diffraction (XRD, a Bruker D8 Advance) between 5° and 65° (2θ) with CuKα1 (λ1 = 0.15406 nm) at 40 KV and 40 mA. To discuss the effects of copper and fluoride on the polymorphs of C3S, the regional XRD patterns in the range of 31.5°～33° and 51°～52.5° is necessary [45]. The full XRD patterns could be collected with a 0.02° step width and 1.0 s step time, and the regional XRD patterns were collected with a 0.003° step width and 1.0 s step time.

The microstructure of prepared C3S samples were detected by Hitachi S4800 SEM, and the distribution characteristic of the introduced copper and fluorine in the doped C3S samples were measured by EDS mapping (HORIBA 7593-H).

The binding forms of copper and fluorine in doped C3S samples were unveiled by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) (a Thermo ESCALAB 250XI photoelectron spectrometer) with Mg Kα (hν = 1253.6 eV) X-ray source operating at 16 KV and 14.9 mA. The prepared C3S powders were pressed into a stainless steel sample holder. The data could be collected by a Thermo Avantage Version 5.976 software, and the Shirley background was carried out for the all cases. The XPS spectra was corrected by the charging effects by the adventitious carbon peak C1s line with the binding energy 284.8 eV, in addition, and the built-in XPS Knowledge View of Thermo Avantage software. The NIST X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Database (Website available) could be the key analysis tools [46].

The hydration heat evolution of doped C3S would be monitored by an isothermal heat-conduction calorimetry (TAM air C80, Thermometric, Sweden). The water/solids ratio was 0.50 (deionized water), and the tested samples would be ground into powders to pass through 75 μm sieve and reach about a Blaine surface area of 260～270 m2/kg. In addition, the calorimetric measurements were proceeded at 20 ± 1℃ for about 7 days.

To unveil the effects of fluorine and copper on burnability of doped C3S samples, the f-CaO contents were measured, and the results were depicted in Fig. 1 . It is indicated that the f-CaO content of undoped C3S was high as 0.9345%, yet, the addition of CaF2 could well better the burnability to reduce the f-CaO content, and the f-CaO content of the doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 reached 0.1726%. The above results demonstrated the melting and mineralization effect of fluoride [36]. It is interesting to find that a trace of CuO was incorporated into CaF2 doped C3S could prominently decrease the f-CaO content for an excellent burnability. The results showed that the f-CaO content of the doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2 and 0.25% CuO reduced by 46.64% compared with 1.00% CaF2 doped C3S, and the f-CaO content of the doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and 1.00% CuO even reach 0.0054%. It could be found that the combined addition of CaF2 and CuO had the distinct cooperation effects on the burnability beyond single addition of CaF2 or CuO [13].

The immobilization of Cu and F in the doped C3S samples were described in Table 3 . The results showed that the immobilization ratios of Cu and F were all above 99% in these doped samples, and the more addition of CaF2 make more immobilization ratios of F. In addition, the incorporation of a few amounts of CuO into doped C3S with CaF2 could slightly stimulate the immobilization of F and Cu. Thus, incorporating CuO into C3S doped with CaF2 could simultaneously promote the immobilization of hazardous element F and Cu, and its promotion might result from the change of the liquid-state phase properties by the cooperation effects of CaF2 and CuO [18].

ce:section.ce:section-title: Mineral compositions of doped C3S and C3S polymorphisms
ce:section.ce:para: It is recognized that the different C3S polymorphisms include triclinic (T1, T2 and T3), monoclinic (M1and M3) and rhombohedral (R) could be identified by the regional XRD patterns in the 2θ ranges of 31.5°～33° and 51°～52.5° [47,48], additionally, the hydration and mechanical properties of C3S with different polymorphism might be further improved or weakened [49,50]. Therefore, it is necessary to discuss the effects of CaF2 and CuO on the mineral compositions and polymorphisms revealed by XRD with various scanning parameters. Fig. 2 presented full XRD patterns of doped C3S samples, the built-in figures were characteristic diffraction positions of polymorphisms. Then Table 4 summarized the main mineral compositions and C3S polymorphisms of these doped samples.

The results in Fig. 2 indicated that the main mineral composition in these samples were only alite without other minerals even in the doped samples with 2.00% CaF2 and 1.00% CuO after successive calcination under 1500℃. It implied that the addition of CaF2 and CuO into C3S would not alter the final mineral compositions. In the meantime, the diffraction intensity of alite came to be stronger with more addition of CaF2, it stated that the addition of CaF2 would benefit to promote the alite formation and improve its crystallizability [16]. It was found that the more addition of CuO into doped C3S with CaF2 could lead to the stronger diffraction of alite, its crystallizability might be further promoted by small amounts of CuO addition as well.

It could be noticed in Fig. 2 that three diffraction peaks in the range of 31.5°～33°, and other three peaks in the range of 51°～52.5° of undoped C3S sample, it is a typical characteristics of triclinic T3 form with relatively low symmetric C3S crystal structure [42]. The structural symmetry of the doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2 increased as the polymorphism coexistence of T3 and monoclinic M1, and its main polymorphism was identified as M1 form [47]. A little addition of 0.25% CuO could also promote the structural symmetry even though the C3S presented the polymorphism coexistence of T3 and M1, the characteristic of M1 came to clearer. With the addition of CuO increasing to 0.50%, its structural symmetry became higher with monoclinic M3 form [49]. However, it was worth noting that the symmetry started to reduce from M3 to M1 with the addition of CuO increasing to 1.00%. The results in Table 4 indicated that the structural symmetry of doped C3S samples all would increase with CaF2 (≤2.00%) and CuO (＜1.00%) addition increasing, but its symmetry would be lowered as the addition of CuO was 1.00%. Ma et al. [13] once reported that the excessive addition of 3.00% CuO in doped clinker induced R C3S gradually transform into M3 with reduction of symmetry. Thus, the incorporation of CuO and CaF2 into C3S would accelerate the symmetry reduction only with 1.00% addition of CuO.

ce:section.ce:section-title: Microstructure and element distributions of doped C3S
ce:section.ce:para: The cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on the microstructure of doped C3S were revealed in Fig. 3 , Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 . Fig. 3 indicated that the internal structure of the undoped C3S was quite porous with small crystalline grains, its crystalline mainly grew together with each other, and it presented a slow growth trend from inside to outside due to the poor high temperature reaction environment, additionally, the surface of the crystals was smooth without defects, and the interface was clear. It could be conjectured that the formation of C3S was quietly difficult without the fluxing materials [16], and its formation would only depend on the solid state reaction between C2S and CaO.

The results in Fig. 4 showed that the internal structure became compact after adding 2.00% CaF2, and the size of crystalline grains became big, however, its surface came to be rough with obvious defects that might be caused by the accelerated iterative growth of new crystals on primary crystals, the interface between crystals was also vague. It stated that the formation of C3S was accelerated with CaF2, but the crystal defects were increased. The microstructure of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and 1.00% CuO in Fig. 5 showed that the formation of C3S was further promoted by the cooperation of CaF2 and CuO, its calcined structure was more compact, and the crystals continuously grew to be a big conjoined body, the defects on the crystals were easy to find as well.

To explore the distribution characteristics of fluorine and copper in the doped C3S after calcination, EDS was used in this paper. Fig. 6 and Fig. 7 were element distribution maps of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and 1.00% CuO, respectively. Every element has a different color, and its brightness of that stands for the relatively contents of every element in selected areas. Fig. 6 showed that F element was more likely to be concentrated at the interface of C3S grains, and its distribution characteristic might relate with the changes of the hydration process of CaF2 doped C3S [38]. The distribution maps of F, Cu, O and Ca elements in Fig. 7 indicated that the distribution of F was more concentrated than that of Cu, the distribution of Cu was quite dispersed, and a few of Cu were also concentrated in the interface of C3S grains.

ce:section.ce:section-title: Binding forms of fluorine and copper in doped C3S
ce:section.ce:para: To figure out the difference of the distribution characteristics between fluorine and copper in the doped C3S, and to understand the chemical valence states of fluorine and copper, the binding forms of fluorine and copper were analysed by XPS. The survey spectral and F spectral of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 were showed in Fig. 8 (a) and (b), the survey spectral, F spectral and Cu spectral of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and 1.00% CuO were showed in Fig. 9 (a), (b) and (c). Fig. 8 revealed that fluorine only had a one Gaussian fitting peak F1s at binding energy of 684.6 eV in narrow spectrum, it was well corresponding to the F- in Ca-F bond [46], and any other minerals containing F could not be detected in the doped C3S by regional XRD rescanning, it means that addition of CaF2 less than 2.00% would not reach its incorporation solution limits into C3S [25]. Therefore, F- of CaF2 would likely enter C3S structure by the replacement of O2– of C3S to combine with Ca2+. The above findings would result in the defects of C3S crystal lattice, and thereupon the C3S characteristic diffraction peaks might come to shift right.

Fig. 9 demonstrated that a Gaussian fitting peak of fluorine was noticed at binding energy of 684.6 eV as F1s, which meant that the co-addition of Cu into C3S could not interfere the binding forms of F in doped C3S. Copper in doped C3S had two Cu 2p3/2 (933.1 eV) and Cu 2p1/2 (952.9 eV) main Gaussian fitting peaks with a visible satellite Gaussian fitting peak in the range of 940.0 eV～945.0 eV, it was corresponding to the Cu2+ of Cu–O bond [46], in addition, any other minerals containing F or Cu also could not be detected in the doped C3S by regional XRD rescanning, it also means that CaF2 and CuO would not reach their incorporation solution limits into C3S [25]. Therefore, F- would also likely enter the C3S structure, Cu2+ would possibly enter C3S structure by substituting Ca2+ due to its similar electrochemical properties between Cu2+ and Ca2+ [18,52]. The above results could verify the distinct right shifting of C3S characteristic diffraction peaks.

ce:section.ce:section-title: Hydration heat evolution of doped C3S
ce:section.ce:para: The cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on the hydration characteristics of doped C3S were revealed by hydration heat evolution in Fig. 10 , Fig. 11 and Fig. 12 . The hydration heat evolution of doped C3S in Fig. 10 showed that a rapid exothermic peak arrived in the initial period within 10 min, it mainly rely on the dissolution rate of alite [53]. The addition of CaF2 accelerated the initial hydration rate, and heat flow of doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2 could reach 0.115 W/g, while it was 0.091 W/g of undoped C3S. The accelerated initial hydration might origin from the increase hydration active points caused by the change of microstructure and defects on the surface of alite [54]. In the next induction period, it could be found that CaF2 prolonged the induction period, and its duration reached 7.78 h, 7.80 h and even 38.3 h with the addition of CaF2 increasing, besides, the highest heat flow in the acceleration period was reduced markedly due to addition of CaF2. Hence, CaF2 addition could prolong the induction period, postpone the acceleration period, and decrease the later hydration rates of doped C3S. The results in Fig. 10 (b) showed that the cumulative heat release of C3S in the induction period was increased by CaF2 addition, and then the cumulative heat release would be always lower than that of undoped C3S. As for the changes of hydration process of C3S caused by CaF2 addition might result from the accelerated initial hydration due to the changed microstructure and increased defects [55], and began to form a relatively dense layer of the initial hydration products on the surface of unhydrated C3S, and then distinctly hinder the further hydration of doped C3S [39], besides, the characteristics of the initial hydration products containing F of CaF2 doped C3S may differ from that of the undoped C3S, and it would also interfere the subsequent hydration reaction of doped C3S [56].

The hydration heat evolution of doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2 and different amounts of CuO in Fig. 11 demonstrated that an obvious exothermic peak existed after contacting water in about 10 min, and the initial hydration rates were quite higher than that of doped with 1.00% CaF2. With the addition of CuO increasing, it would gradually increase as 0.165 W/g, 0.166 W/g and 0.186 W/g. The addition of CuO into doped C3S with CaF2 directly promoted the initial hydration rate possibly due to its increased surface defects and the change of microstructures [57]. The duration of induction period shortened with the addition of CuO with different degrees, and in the acceleration period, its hydration heat flow was much higher than the doped C3S without CuO. The results in Fig. 11 (b) indicated that the cumulative heat release of doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2 and different amounts of CuO in the induction period were quite higher than that of doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2, in the next periods, the cumulative heat release of doped C3S would always be higher than that of doped C3S with 1.00% CaF2. Therefore, it could be noted that the small incorporation of CuO into CaF2 doped C3S presented the apparent cooperation effects on the hydration process, the addition of CuO accompanied with CaF2 shortened the induction period, advanced the acceleration period, and increased its hydration rates.

The hydration heat evolution of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2 and CuO in Fig. 12 testified that the initial hydration could be promoted by the addition of 2.00% CaF2 and CuO, and its heat flow reached 0.182 W/g, 0.174 W/g, and 0.174 W/g with the addition of CuO increasing. Even though the duration of the induction period came to lessen as 16.98 h, 23.05 h and 57.80 h compared with that of doped C3S with 2.00% CaF2, the hydration heat flow was seriously hindered when the addition of CuO was more than 0.50%, while the addition of CuO below 0.25% would shorten the induction period, advance the acceleration period, and increase its hydration rates. The addition of CuO beyond 0.50% sharply reduced the hydration heat flow of the doped C3S.

Tao et al. [58] once discussed the retardation mechanisms caused by CuO that Cu2+ might be more competitive than Ca2+ of the doped C3S for nucleophilic attacks during the hydration process, it was due to the relatively lower Cu3d orbitals to obtain electrons easily from anions OH– released by H2O, and the prior hydroxylation of Cu2+ will reduce the concentration of OH– in the hydrated solution to further delay the oversaturation of portlandite and the other hydration products. Additionally, the changed characteristics of the initial hydration products containing F and Cu might change the later hydration process of the doped C3S [13]. However, it might need more confirmations by intuitive methods to explain the complicated hydration mechanisms of doped C3S with CaF2 and CuO.

In this work, the cooperation effects of fluorine and copper on the formation and properties of prepared C3S were revealed by XRD, SEM-EDS, XPS and isothermal heat flow calorimetry. The following findings could be obtained.

Although CaF2 reduced f-CaO content of C3S and improved its burnability, a small cooperation addition of CuO only as 0.25% could reduce distinctly f-CaO content of C3S, and its burnability was substantially promoted. The cooperation effects of CaF2 and CuO strengthened the immobilization of fluorine and copper in doped C3S matrix.

The cooperation addition of CaF2 and CuO into C3S enhanced the formation and growth of alite grains, and ensured C3S polymorphisms with higher structural symmetry keep stable at room temperature. The characteristic diffraction peaks of C3S shifted to the larger angles with the co-addition of CaF2 and CuO. The cooperation addition made many defects on the surface of C3S grains visible. Within current incorporation amounts, F- and Cu2+ would dissolve in C3S structure possibly by the replacement of O2– and Ca2+ respectively.

CaF2 addition accelerated the initial hydration, prolonged the induction period, postponed the acceleration period, and decelerated the later hydration of C3S. The initial hydration of C3S was further accelerated by cooperation addition of CuO, and its effects were quite different if changing cooperation amounts of CaF2, at that time, accelerating or decelerating the hydration process of doped C3S would depend on the cooperation amounts of CaF2 and CuO.

We realized the mechanisms about the huge changes of hydration characteristics of doped C3S with F and Cu remain to be confirmed by other measurements, but the current findings in this work might be the valuable foundation to promote the value-added utilization of these hazardous wastes containing Cu in cement kiln. Based on that, we try to apply this cooperation effects to provide a solution on reducing the large CO2 emissions of cement industry.
